title: November 11: Moon — formula-written light-transport weights, inspired by HypaNet
summary: Moon adapts Matthew Gribben's publicly documented idea of AI-authored neural-network weights without gradient descent to a new translucent quasicrystal-moon transport problem. It is an independent scene and implementation, not a demonstrated fork of HypaNet or CrystalMoonV3. Its source-reported held-back camera/sun tests are promising within one fixed medium, but two constants were manually selected using reference views; generalization beyond that scene and independent replication remain open. Gribben's HypaNet code is MIT-licensed; retained original copyright/notice is required for any copied substantial code.

nodes.claim: Hand-Written Moon: a translucent quasicrystal-sphere light-transport network whose weights are generated deterministically from radiative-transfer formulas, without gradient-descent training. Inspired by Matthew Gribben's HypaNet written-weight research, but with a different target scene, custom reference tracer, analytic network construction and browser shader.
nodes.survived: The README reports mean relative luminance error of 7.1% on 12 reference camera/sun views and 7.1% on six held-back views for the written all-light network; its compiled and baked browser shader reports 6.7%/6.9%. build_network.py deterministically constructs network.json from analytic formulas. These figures are source-reported, not independently rerun by Genealogy.
nodes.killed: The 7.1% error is scene-specific and not directly comparable to HypaNet's cloud benchmark or previous CrystalMoon physics. BETA=0.6 and LAM=0.7 were hand-set against reference views, so 'no training' means no gradient/optimiser, not no empirical calibration. Only one density medium is tested; no general transport solver, learned weights, new quasicrystal growth law or code inheritance from CrystalMoonV3 has been established.

edges.why: Both projects explore quasicrystal-moon imagery and illumination, but CrystalMoonV3 simulates RGB-responsive crystal growth while Moon constructs a fixed-scene radiative-transfer neural network; no code fork, shared model weights or demonstrated computational inheritance is claimed. Moon directly credits Matthew Gribben's external HypaNet work as conceptual inspiration.

motifs.title: A physically written network is not a learned world or a grown material
motifs.description: Moon explicitly encodes a physics approximation in fixed neural weights, while CrystalMoonV3 lets illumination affect a simulated crystal texture. Similar lunar visuals do not imply shared code or dynamics. Moon's 12/6 reference and held-back camera/sun conditions test view generality within one medium, not out-of-scene generality; manual scalar calibration is distinct from gradient-descent training.
